note: Live rounds fired at the harness itself. Each one is a small edit that makes the rig fail open in a specific way; verify-self applies it, puts the fixed situation in rig/self_probe.mjs through the edited rig, and demands the answer change. A round that leaves the answer untouched means the harness is blind at that point, and the run leaves as SELF-BLIND with every other number declared void. This is a floor and not a proof: it covers the ways of going blind that were thought of. The drift line on the report is the standing admission of that.

meta_breaches.breaks: an empty population with no recorded reason is reported as a pass
a reading whose requirement is absent is folded into the passes
the report digest stops depending on the report, so two different runs look identical
meta_breaches.expect: the probe digest stops tracking the probe

meta_breaches.breaks: a run that never reached a real server becomes eligible for green

edits.find: else if (tally.skip > 0 || !wire) { outcome = OUTCOME.PARTIAL; exit = EXIT.PARTIAL; }
edits.replace: else if (tally.skip > 0) { outcome = OUTCOME.PARTIAL; exit = EXIT.PARTIAL; }

meta_breaches.expect: the wireless gate stops reading PARTIAL

meta_breaches.breaks: a reading nothing has ever been fired at stops making the run red
meta_breaches.expect: the unarmed gate stops reading RED

meta_breaches.expect: registration stops refusing an assay with no tier -- and it takes two edits to get there, which is why the edits array has no ceiling
